addendum: GATE1 Addendum A3 — pairContext channel: RATIFIED (A), AMENDED — 2026-09-17
source: security/PROJECTS/computercaller/e2e/GATE1-ADDENDUM-A3.md, section 'Vector I'. Computed by Security in an independent HKDF/GCM implementation (a3-vectors-verify.mjs). Transcribed VERBATIM — never regenerated from P4's own code, which is the implementation under test. All three positive/negative key values were additionally re-derived from the addendum text before being committed.
note: A3 says ADD vector I to tests/kdf-vectors.json. Same reason as kdf-vectors-a2.json: androidTest/resources/kdf-vectors.json is the byte-identical copy whose sha256 is the (c3) cross-lane proof, and the android lane must not edit the web lane's canonical file. Flagged to Ken for P0.2.
assertion: wire ctx + LOCAL userId == the frozen local context, byte for byte. P4 asserts this through its ENCODE path (it builds ctx); P2/P3 assert through their DECODE path. That pairing is what makes vector I cross-implementation rather than two copies of one belief.

I2_negative_epoch_drift.requirement: A2 vector F's ciphertext MUST FAIL AUTHENTICATION under this key/prefix — the A3-M2 replay case.

I3_negative_userid_drift.requirement: One character of a NEVER-TRANSMITTED field diverges the key totally — proves userId is load-bearing and that a session-identity mismatch fails closed.

I4_parser_negatives.requirement: All MUST throw/refuse at ctx ingest, never coerce.
I4_parser_negatives.strictness: A3 rejects above 2^64-1; P4 rejects above 2^63-1 (Long.MAX_VALUE). Stricter, and deliberately so: pairEpoch is a count of Accepts by one phone, so 2^63 is unreachable, while a value above it would have to be carried as a negative Long and every downstream be64/AAD assertion would then be reasoning about a sign bit. Refusing is fail-closed; coercing would not be.
I4_parser_negatives.alsoRejected: ctx absent on a mode=1 block; peerDeviceId != own deviceId; any of userId/phoneDeviceId/peerDeviceId over 255 UTF-8 bytes
